It has further been alleged that in the meantime, PO 88 of 1972 was promulgated which section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act has incorporated by which the sale with separate agreement for re-conveyance became usufrucuary mortgage. The plaintiff alleged that the transaction was a mortgage and lastly requested on 25-4-1991 to get back the suit land but no effect. Hence the suit. 

 4. The suit was contested by the defendant petitioner by filing written statement denying all the material averment made in the plaint contending inter-alia that the transaction is an out and sale and does not come within the mischief of PO 88 of 1972 as the alleged transfer with agreement for re-conveyance was made dated 23-3-1967 and subsistence of the agreement was for two years only and after expiry of the fixed dated i.e. on 22-3-1969 alleged agreement for sale is to be treated as past and closed transaction so the sale in question became absolute before the promulgation of PO 88 of 1972 and, as such, which cannot be redempt. It has also been arrested that the suit property is non-agricultural property situated within Narayanganj Municipality and so section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act is not applicable in this case. The defendant 'has strongly asserted that the plaintiff has never offered: to repay the consideration money within agreed period for getting, back the property, so the sale has become absolute and the agreement became past and closed transaction. Thus the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 8. Mr FM Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that both the courts erred in law in not considering the material facts and circumstances of the case. The learned Advocate further submitted that whether a transaction is a sale or mortgage would be decided by the court mainly on the basis of the recital of the main deed not on the basis of the separate agreement signed by the defendant alone but both the courts below decreed the suit without considering the main deed signed by the predecessor of the plaintiff. He further submitted that on perusal of the said deed it is found that the executants sold the land to the defendant by receiving entire consideration money and which is an out and out sale deed not a mortgage deed. The learned Advocate further submitted that usufructuary mortgage only depend on the provision of Section 2 (6) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and by observing the conditions laid down in the said section. In support of his argument he referred the case of Abdul Hafiz Chowdhury vs Somor Ali reported in 4 DLR 126. The learned Advocate further submitted that the usufructuary mortgage is only for agricultural land but the suit land is a homestated situated within the municipal area so it cannot be redempt under Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In support of his argument he referred the case of Shahjahan Mizi vs Md Shamsul Haque Mizi report in 3 BLC 528. The learned Advocate further submitted that without taking loan money question of mortgage is not acceptable and in this case the plaintiff neither mentioned in the plaint that the executants took loan from the defendant nor it is stated in the main deed and, as such, the impugned transaction cannot be a mortgage. The learned Advocate further submitted that the impugned transaction is a past and closed transaction because the agreement was for two years and the period having been expired in the year 1969 and the transaction between the parties undisputedly came to an end before the promulgation of president order No. 88 of 1972 which came into force on 3-8-1972. In support he referred the decision of the case of Asmat Ali vs Abdur Rafique Mridha reported in 52 DLR (AD) 132 and the case of Abu Bakkar vs Nazir Ahmed reported in 34 DLR (AD) 237. Thus, he prayed for making the Rule absolute. 

 9. On the contrary, Mr Md Ziaul Haque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties submitted that both the courts after considering the evidence on record and the facts and circumstances of the case decreed the suit and the concurrent finding of fact cannot be interfered with in revisional jurisdiction under Section 115 (1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned Advocate further submitted that as per Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy act mortgage should be applicable for all categories of land including holding or house or building. He further submitted that in the instant case it is clear that the petitioner executed a re-conveyance deed on the same sitting through a separate deed which should be treated as complete usufructuary mortgage. In support he reliance the case of Asmat Ali vs Abdur Rafiq Mridha reported in 52 DLR (AD) 132. The learned Advocate further submitted that if the plaintiff succeed to prove that there is an agreement of re-conveyance in such a case the said agreement should be treated as complete usufructuary mortgage and the petitioner can file redemption case within 60 years as per Article 148 of the Limitation Act. The learned Advocate further submitted that on close reading of Sub-Section 16 of Section 2 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, Section 95A of the State Acquisition of Tenancy Act, PO 88 of 1972, PO 137 of 1972 and PO 24 of 1973 the claimed land is to be treated as complete usufructuary mortgage which supported by the decisions reported in 34 DLR (AD) 237, 52 DLR (AD) 132, 36 DLR (AD) 90, 49 DLR 172, and 49 DLR (AD) 71. Thus, he prayed for discharging the Rule. 

 12. In the case of Shahjahan Mizi vs Md Shamsul Hoque Mizi reported in 3 BLC 528 a single bench of this court opined that the mortgage is applicable only in the case of Agricultural land. But the Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act defines usufructuary mortgage which is reproduced as below: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any transfer of a holding or of portion or share thereof [either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey, [for] where the transferor receives from the transferee any consideration and the transferee acquires the right to possess, and to enjoy the usufruct of such holding or portion or share thereof for a specified period in lieu of such consideration, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provisions of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Amendment) Order, 1972] (President's Order No. 88 of 1972). 

 14. It appears that the deed was executed on 23-3-1967 and on the same day i.e. on same sitting a separate agreement of reconveyance was executed. As per decision of the case of Asmat Ali vs Abdur Rafique Mridha reported in 52 DLR (AD) 132 it is settled that any transfer with a re-conveyance should be treated as mortgage. Though in the instant case it is found that the said matter was not stated in the deed of transfer but on the same day the another re-conveyance deed was executed and wherein it is clearly stated that if the executants pay the said amount within two years the property will be returned back to the executant. 

 15. On close reading of the Section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act it is clear that the transfer deed executed on 23-3-1967 is a mortgage deed. Though it is found that Section 58 (C) of the TP Act does not mention the same but ultimately Section 95A clearly provides that mortgage is applicable in all the holdings including house or building or any portion or share. So the deed dated 23-3-1967 is a mortgage deed not out and out sale deed. In the case of Abu Bakkar vs Nazir Ahmed reported in 34 DLR (AD) 237 it is settled that once it is proved mortgage always a mortgage not a past and closed transaction.
